legend: It is a sunny day on Columbia campus, and Alice and Bob decide to go to Butler Lawns to play their favorite game: Permutation Game. Since the weather is so nice, Alice wants to stay on the lawns as long as possible, while Bob has a midterm the next day and wants to get home to study.
Permutation Game is played as follows:
Alice receives a permutation a$$$a$$$ and Bob receives a permutation b$$$b$$$, both of size n$$$n$$$∗$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$.
Alice chooses an index i$$$i$$$ (1≤i≤n$$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$) and places a token on position i$$$i$$$ of her permutation a$$$a$$$.
Bob, after seeing where Alice has placed her token, chooses an index j$$$j$$$ (1≤j≤n$$$1 \leq j \leq n$$$) and places his own token on position j$$$j$$$ of his permutation b$$$b$$$.
Alice and Bob each follow their permutation one step at a time:   Alice moves her token to index ai$$$a_i$$$, then aai$$$a_{a_i}$$$, and so on.
Bob moves his token to index bj$$$b_j$$$, then bbj$$$b_{b_j}$$$, and so on.

∗$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A permutation of length n$$$n$$$ is an array consisting of n$$$n$$$ distinct integers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ in arbitrary order. For example, [2$$$2$$$, 3$$$3$$$, 1$$$1$$$, 5$$$5$$$, 4$$$4$$$] is a permutation, but [1$$$1$$$, 2$$$2$$$, 2$$$2$$$] is not a permutation (2$$$2$$$ appears twice in the array), and [1$$$1$$$, 3$$$3$$$, 4$$$4$$$] is also not a permutation (n=3$$$n = 3$$$ but there is a 4$$$4$$$ in the array).
input: The first line of input contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
The second line of input contains n$$$n$$$ distinct integers a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1, a_2, ..., a_n$$$ — Alice's permutation a$$$a$$$.
The third line of input contains n$$$n$$$ distinct integers b1,b2,...,bn$$$b_1, b_2, ...,b_n$$$ — Bob's permutation b$$$b$$$.
output: Output a single integer — the number of steps that will be performed in the game, assuming both players play optimally.
note: In the first sample, regardless of which indices Alice and Bob place their tokens on to start, the process will last for just one step.

In the second example, Alice may place her token at index 3$$$3$$$, and Bob, seeing where Alice has placed her token, places his at index 1$$$1$$$. After one step, Alice's token will be at index 4$$$4$$$ and Bob's will be at index 3$$$3$$$. After two steps, Alice's token will be at index 5$$$5$$$ and Bob's will be at 5$$$5$$$. And after three steps, Alice's token returns to index 3$$$3$$$, while Bob's returns to index 1$$$1$$$.

legend.ai: 哥伦比亚大学校园里阳光明媚，Alice 和 Bob 决定去 Butler Lawns 玩他们最喜欢的游戏：排列游戏。由于天气这么好，Alice 想尽可能久地待在草坪上，而 Bob 第二天有期中考试，想回家学习。
Alice 得到一个排列 a$$$a$$$，Bob 得到一个排列 b$$$b$$$，两者的规模均为 n$$$n$$$∗$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$。
Alice 选择一个下标 i$$$i$$$(1≤i≤n$$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$)，并将一枚棋子放到她的排列 a$$$a$$$ 的位置 i$$$i$$$ 上。
Bob 在看到 Alice 放置棋子的位置后，选择一个下标 j$$$j$$$(1≤j≤n$$$1 \leq j \leq n$$$)，并将自己的棋子放到他的排列 b$$$b$$$ 的位置 j$$$j$$$ 上。
Alice 和 Bob 各自按照自己的排列一步一步移动：Alice 先将棋子移到下标 ai$$$a_i$$$，然后移到 aai$$$a_{a_i}$$$，依此类推。
Bob 将他的棋子移动到下标 bj$$$b_j$$$，然后移动到下标 bbj$$$b_{b_j}$$$，以此类推。

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$)。
输入的第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数 a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1, a_2, ..., a_n$$$——Alice 的排列 a$$$a$$$。
输入的第三行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的整数 b1,b2,...,bn$$$b_1, b_2, ...,b_n$$$——Bob 的排列 b$$$b$$$。

output.ai: 输出一个整数——在双方都采取最优策略的情况下，游戏中将执行的步数。

note.ai: 在第一个样例中，无论 Alice 和 Bob 一开始将自己的棋子放在哪些下标位置，整个过程都只会持续一步。

在第二个样例中，Alice 可以将她的棋子放在下标 3$$$3$$$ 处，而 Bob 看到 Alice 放置棋子的位置后，将自己的棋子放在下标 1$$$1$$$ 处。一步之后，Alice 的棋子会位于下标 4$$$4$$$ 处，而 Bob 的棋子会位于下标 3$$$3$$$ 处。两步之后，Alice 的棋子会位于下标 5$$$5$$$ 处，而 Bob 的棋子会位于下标 5$$$5$$$ 处。三步之后，Alice 的棋子会回到下标 3$$$3$$$ 处，而 Bob 的棋子会回到下标 1$$$1$$$ 处。
